close_reason: Added pub fn new(new_default, previous_default) -> Self mirroring CalendarEventParseResult::new. Purely additive; existing callers continue to work via Default impl + field assignment. Construction-pattern asymmetry within the same file resolved.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:618-630 defines `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct SetDefaultResult` with two `pub` fields and a `Default` impl. It has no `SetDefaultResult::new(new_default, previous_default)` constructor.

Compare the same file: `ParseResult` at :590-606 has an explicit `pub fn new(parsed, not_found, not_parsable)` constructor and the doc-comment at :590-594 cites the rationale: "Required because the struct is #[non_exhaustive] — external crates cannot use struct-literal syntax."

That rationale applies identically to SetDefaultResult: it's `#[non_exhaustive]`, and external backend implementors cannot use struct-literal syntax. They must use `SetDefaultResult::default()` and then assign individual fields (or wait for `..Default::default()` FRU which is forbidden on foreign `#[non_exhaustive]` structs).

The in-crate test_support MockBackend uses struct-literal at lib.rs:828 and :857 — which compiles because it's in-crate, but is exactly the pattern the `#[non_exhaustive]` is supposed to prevent shipping. External consumers do not have this option.

What callers cannot rely on:
- A clear single way to construct a fresh SetDefaultResult with both fields set. (Default::default() then mutate, or some-future-new(), or struct-literal-if-they're-in-crate.)
- That the two sibling result types follow the same construction pattern.

Fix: add `pub fn new(new_default: Option<Id>, previous_default: Option<Id>) -> Self` mirroring ParseResult::new at :595-605. This is purely additive (no SemVer impact).
title: SetDefaultResult missing new() constructor; asymmetric with ParseResult::new in same file
